title: 第 44 課｜莫佩爾蒂原理：只問路徑，不問時間｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
最小作用量原理決定了整個運動：解出運動方程，我們既知道路徑的形狀，也知道什麼時刻走到哪裡。但如果問題比較簡單，只想知道路徑長什麼樣子而不管時間，就可以用一個簡化過的形式。先假設拉格朗日量不顯含時間，所以能量守恆；讓終點的時刻可以變動而位置固定，上一課告訴我們作用量的變分等於負的哈密頓量乘上時刻的變分。現在只比較那些滿足能量守恆的運動，對這些路徑哈密頓量就是常數 E，於是變分關係變成作用量的變分加上 E 乘時刻的變分等於零。把作用量寫成簡略作用量減去 E 乘時間，代進去之後兩項互相抵消，只剩下一句話：簡略作用量的變分等於零。簡略作用量就是動量沿著路徑對座標的積分；所以在所有滿足能量守恆、而且通過終點的路徑裡，不管什麼時候抵達，真實的那一條讓這個積分取極小。要真的用它，必須把動量用座標和座標的微分表示出來，辦法是用動量的定義，再用能量守恆把時間的微分消掉。對通常的拉格朗日量，也就是動能減位能，算出來的結果是簡略作用量等於根號下二倍的能量減位能再乘上動能的二次型。對單個質點，動能是二分之一質量乘速度平方，變分原理就變成根號下二倍質量乘能量減位能沿著路徑長度的積分取極小，這個形式是雅可比給的。自由運動時位能為零，積分就退化成路徑長度，質點走兩點間最短的路，也就是直線；有位能時，根號下能量減位能就扮演光學裡折射率的角色，路徑會彎——力學與幾何光學在這裡完全平行。最後對參數 E 做變分，得到簡略作用量對能量的偏導數等於經過的時間，把時間放回來，路徑與運動就都確定了。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 44 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 44 | Maupertuis' Principle: the Path Without the Time | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
The principle of least action determines the motion completely: solving the equations gives both the shape of the path and the position along it as a function of time. But if the problem is the more restricted one of finding only the path, with no reference to time, a simplified form of the principle can be used. Assume first that the Lagrangian, and so the Hamiltonian, does not contain the time, so the energy is conserved. Letting the final time vary with the coordinates held fixed, the previous lesson gave the variation of the action as minus the Hamiltonian times the variation of the time. Now compare only those motions that satisfy conservation of energy: for such paths the Hamiltonian is the constant E, and the relation becomes the variation of the action plus E times the variation of the time equals zero. Writing the action as the abbreviated action minus E times the time and substituting, the two terms cancel and one statement is left: the variation of the abbreviated action vanishes. The abbreviated action is the integral of momentum along the path, so among all paths that conserve the energy and pass through the final point, whenever they arrive, the true one makes that integral least. To use this we must express the momenta through the coordinates and their differentials, which is done with the definition of momentum, using conservation of energy to eliminate the differential of the time. For the usual Lagrangian, kinetic minus potential energy, the abbreviated action is the integral of the square root of twice the energy minus the potential, times the quadratic form of the kinetic energy. For a single particle the kinetic energy is one-half m v squared, and the principle becomes the integral of the square root of twice the mass times the energy minus the potential, taken along the element of path length; this form is due to Jacobi. In free motion the potential vanishes and the integral is just the path length, so the particle takes the shortest route between two points, a straight line. With a potential, the square root of the energy minus the potential acts exactly as a refractive index and the path bends, so mechanics and geometrical optics run parallel. Finally, varying with respect to the parameter E gives the derivative of the abbreviated action with respect to the energy as the elapsed time, which puts the timing back and completes the motion.

Lesson 44 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
